newsitem.title: USA: US carbon emissions seen at 1.8 bln tonnes by 2015.
newsitem.headline: US carbon emissions seen at 1.8 bln tonnes by 2015.

text.p: U.S. carbon emissions from energy use are expected to rise by 1.2 percent a year to 2015, reaching 1,799 million metric tons, the Energy Information Administration said Wednesday in its annual energy outlook.

The 20-year outlook for carbon pollution was slightly higher than EIA projected last year as it revised down its predictions for oil prices, raised its outlook for energy consumption and lowered its outlook for growth in use of renewable fuels.
The higher emissions projection suggested that unless the Clinton administration took new steps, it would not meet its goal of reducing U.S. greenhouse gas emissions to 1990 levels by 2000.
The price, supply and demand outlook, released in November, pegged oil prices in 2015 at $21 a barrel in 1995 dollars and consumption at 22 million barrels per day (bpd).
By 2015 petroleum is expected to be the source of 747 million tons of carbon emissions, up from 599 million tons in 1995, holding a steady share of about 42 percent of total U.S. carbon emissions.

Carbon emissions from coal are expected to climb to 607 million tons in 2015 from 507 million tons in 1995, but coal's share of total carbon emissions is expected to shrink to 34 percent from 36 percent.

Burning of natural gas is expected to make up an increasing share of carbon pollution, rising to 25 percent in 2015 up from 22 percent in 1995 as emissions grow to 444 million tons from 318 million tons.
